Photograph: Alamy Pesticides Almost half of world’s farmers poisoned by pesticides every year, experts find Study reveals that pesticide poisoning kills 11,000 people each year, with India accounting for nearly 60% of fatalities Pippa Neill Environment reporter Wed 2 Sep 2026 02.00 EDT Last modified on Wed 2 Sep 2026 02.01 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Almost half of the world’s farmers are poisoned by pesticides every single year, a study has found. Using publicly available data from 2006-2023, the study, which was commissioned by Pesticide Action Network , found there to be an estimated 402-433m cases of unintentional acute pesticide poisoning of farmers and farm workers every year. Based on a worldwide farming population of 934 million, this means approximately 46% of farmers are being poisoned every year. The greatest estimated number of poisonings was in southern Asia, followed by south-east Asia and east Africa . The overall highest national incidence of poisoning was in Burkina Faso in west Africa, where nearly 84% of farmers and farm workers were reported to have experienced poisoning. View image in fullscreen Young farm workers harvesting cotton in a field near Boromo in Burkina Faso. Photograph: Issouf Sanogo/AFP/Getty The study, published in the journal Frontiers in Public Health on Wednesday, also found that an estimated 11,000 deaths occur every year due to pesticide poisoning, with nearly 60% of these in India. Jayakumar Chelaton, the executive director of Pesticide Action Network India , said the research exposed a “crisis that can no longer be ignored”. The authors of the study are calling for “immediate action”, including the implementation of a UN recommendation to phase out highly hazardous pesticides. The study states that despite global efforts to highlight the dangers, pesticide use has continued to grow steadily, with 3.8m tonnes used in 2023, a doubling since 1990. Dr Sheila Willis, the head of international programmes at Pesticide Action Network UK, said: “Now that the scale of suffering has been revealed, farmers must be supported to access safer alternatives to protect their health and that of their families.” The study did not consider the impact of pesticide exposure on the estimated 84 million children working in agriculture and did not look at the long-term health impacts, with acute pesticide poisoning defined in the study as any illness or health effect experienced a short time after exposure. skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Down to Earth The planet's most important stories. Get all the week's environment news - the good, the bad and the essential after newsletter promotion California bans paraquat, highly toxic herbicide outlawed in more than 70 countries Read more Génon Jensen, the executive director of the Health and Environment Alliance, said: “We are extremely concerned about the devastating health impacts from pesticide poisonings – both the acute impacts mentioned in this study but also chronic exposures that farm workers and communities suffer.” Hélène Nicora, the director general of Parkinson’s Europe, said there was also “overwhelming evidence” to suggest that Parkinson’s was an environmentally driven disease, with growing evidence linking pesticide exposure to the development of Parkinson’s. Parkinson’s disease is a progressive disorder in which parts of the brain become damaged over time, affecting movement and balance. The global burden of the disease is rising, with France, Germany and Italy all recognising it as an occupational disease for farmers . Farmers and farm workers are mainly exposed to pesticides during preparation and application, as well as when touching treated crops and contaminated equipment or clothing. Speaking at a webinar organised by Friends of the Earth Europe earlier this year, Rendert Algra said he believed his Parkinson’s disease was linked to the pesticides he had used when working at his family farm in the Netherlands. “Being the eldest son, I did all the spraying of pesticides in our fields for several years in a row,” he said. Despite being the most robust study to date, the report highlights that available information on pesticide poisoning is inadequate, with the authors calling for standardised surveillance and reporting protocols so that pesticide-related poisonings become reliable and comparable. https://www.digi24.ro/stiri/externe/cele.text: Cinci ţări europene, printre care Franţa, Germania şi Regatul Unit, vor reprezenta Europa la viitoarele tratative privind Ucraina, a anunţat vineri un responsabil european, citat de AFP. Prezent la Dublin, președintele Nicușor Dan a spus că „aceste discuţii nu trebuie să aibă de a face cu arhitectura de securitate a Europei, ci doar strict cu războiul din Ucraina”. Polonia, Italia şi reprezentanţi ai Comisiei Europene şi ai Consiliului European vor completa această echipă, a precizat responsabilul citat. El a dat asigurări că acest format a fost validat de şefii de stat sau de guvern ai statelor din Uniunea Europeană în timpul summitului informal de la Dublin. Potrivit Reuters, liderii statelor UE au afirmat că structura securităţii Europei nu ar trebui să fie un subiect al negocierilor de pace între Kiev şi Moscova. Kremlinul a declarat vineri că Rusia ar fi deschisă ideii ca ţările europene să ia parte la convorbirile de pace privind Ucraina dacă ele sunt pregătite să contribuie la procesul de pace. Cancelarul german Friedrich Merz a descris comentariile Rusiei drept „acelaşi vechi joc” şi a subliniat că Europa şi SUA au căzut de acord asupra unui mesaj clar. „Nu vor exista discuţii despre Ucraina fără Ucraina şi discuţii despre Europa fără Europa. Mai mult, nu este nicio nevoie de discuţii despre arhitectura de securitate europeană. Avem deja aşa ceva”, a declarat Merz în faţa jurnaliştilor în timpul summitului UE de la Dublin. Şefa diplomaţiei europene, Kaja Kallas, a accentuat că solicitările Rusiei de a discuta despre arhitectura securităţii europene riscă să abată atenţia de la nevoia de încetare a focului în Ucraina. Premierul leton Andris Kulbergs a calificat aceste discuţii drept „o capcană”. În timpul unei întâlniri desfăşurate joi la Dublin, lideri din Polonia, ţările baltice şi statele nordice au avertizat cu privire la eventuale discuţii cu SUA sau Rusia despre arhitectura securităţii europene, potrivit unui diplomat şi unei oficialităţi europene. Liderii a 40 de ţări europene, reuniţi în capitala irlandeză în cadrul summitului Comunităţii Politice Europene, au semnat o declaraţie ce arată că orice chestiune ce afectează securitatea europeană ar trebui să fie decisă cu implicarea europenilor. Reprezentanţi ai Regatului Unit, Germaniei, Italiei şi UE au participat la discuţiile ruso-americane de la Abu Dhabi în această săptămână, unde atât Moscova, cât şi Kievul au evocat unele progrese, deşi nu există semnale pozitive privind chestiunile esenţiale, precum teritoriul. Preşedintele Nicuşor Dan a declarat, vineri, la Dublin, după reuniunea informală a Consiliului European, că în ceea ce priveşte recentele negocieri cu privire la războiul din Ucraina, s-a stabilit de principiu că e util ca Europa să fie parte din aceste discuţii dar aceste discuţii nu trebuie să aibă de a face cu arhitectura de securitate a Europei, ci doar strict cu războiul din Ucraina. Preşedintele Nicuşor Dan a declarat la finalul Consiliului European informal care a avut loc la Dublin, în Irlanda, că a fost şi o discuţie legată de, mai generală, de securitate şi evident legată de războiul din Ucraina şi de recentele negocieri. Poti actualiza setarile modulelor coookie direct din browser sau de aici – e nevoie sa accepti cookie-urile social media „Evident, poziţia noastră cu privire la Marea Neagră este cunoscută şi interesul de a o proteja cu toate elementele şi militare, şi diplomatice, şi de informaţii. Iar în ceea ce priveşte recentele negocieri cu privire la războiul din Ucraina, a existat, cum am spus, o discuţie de principiu. Am stabilit de principiu că e util ca Europa să fie parte din aceste discuţii”, a precizat şeful statului. El a mai afirmat că „s-a stabilit în mod unanim că aceste discuţii nu trebuie să aibă de a face cu arhitectura de securitate a Europei, ci doar strict cu războiul din Ucraina, inclusiv cu garanţiile de securitate din faza de după terminarea războiului”. „Şi pentru Uniunea Europeană şi pentru Coaliţia de Voinţă s-a stabilit cine să participe la aceste discuţii, urmând ca, dacă ele vor avea loc, urmând ca ulterior deciziile să fie luate în interiorul celor două organisme, Uniunea Europeană şi Coaliţia de Voinţă.” Urmărește știrile Digi24.ro și pe Google News

https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c6wy.text: Image source, Getty Images Image caption, More than a million people were forced to flee the violence across the border to Bangladesh in 2017 By Tom McArthur Published 6 hours ago The UK has sanctioned five senior Myanmar military leaders after the International Court of Justice (ICJ) ruled that the country had carried out genocide against the Rohingya minority â marking the first time a state has been found guilty of the crime . A military crackdown in 2017 killed thousands of Rohingya and forced more than 700,000 to flee Buddhist-majority Myanmar, formerly known as Burma. The UK is joined by several other countries , external in acknowledging the ICJ ruling, including Australia, Belgium, Portugal, Spain and Canada. Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband said: "Our response to a crime as profoundly shocking as genocide must reflect our values and must be matched by clear action." Bowen: Myanmar genocide verdict is historic and could have far-reaching implications Published 4 days ago How do you define genocide? Published 4 April 2022 The senior military leaders facing sanctions are Myo Htut Hlaing, Myo Min Tun, Myat Thet Oo, Kyaw Soe and Kyaw Swar Oo. Miliband added that Myanmar's President Min Aung Hlaing , who was sanctioned by the UK in 2021, is "directly responsible for many of the atrocities that have happened" as he was head of the military at the time of the genocide in 2017. He said: "Myanmar must stop ongoing violations, investigate, prosecute and punish perpetrators, and prevent such an atrocity from ever happening again." Miliband also called for an "immediate pause in hostilities to enable humanitarian aid to get through, a stop to air strikes on civilians, and the release of political prisoners, as well as dialogue towards an inclusive political settlement". The foreign secretary confirmed that new legislation would be passed to stop the supply of aviation fuel to the country, which was known as Burma until 1989. Last week, he expelled Myanmar's defence attachÃ© after the ICJ ruled the country had committed genocide during the brutal military campaign in 2017. He told MPs on Monday the UK would raise the issue at the UN Security Council this week, and there would be a dedicated meeting in a fortnight. The court found on Thursday that "genocidal intent is the only reasonable inference that can be drawn from the evidence" it had seen. The verdict was reached by a majority of nine votes to six among a panel of judges from around the world. The ICJ also found in favour by majority that Myanmar had violated several other parts of the 1948 Genocide Convention , external . In its ruling last week, the court determined that about 10,000 Rohingya were murdered during the clearance operation in the western Rakhine state that borders Bangladesh and the Bay of Bengal. Myanmar denied the claims against it. Reports said that entire villages were burnt down, and that women and girls were raped. Miliband said more than 1.2 million refugees fled and were being supported by Bangladesh. Myanmar's leader during the genocide, Aung San Suu Kyi , was deposed by the military in 2021. MPs heard that air strikes and violence from the Arakan army were still happening.
